home.faq.a1: They never pass through Clair. You authenticate on your bank's own site, which issues a read-only access in return — stored encrypted, time-limited, and revocable at any moment. Access goes through TrueLayer, authorised for account information across Europe.
home.faq.a2: The list shown when connecting is authoritative. It depends on your country, account type and banking provider availability. Institutions on this page are illustrative; demo accounts are fictional.
home.faq.a3: An operation's label after masking, its amount and its currency — never a third-party name, an IBAN or a reference. It files an expense and answers your questions; no financial calculation is delegated to it, and it can change nothing.
home.faq.a4: From your account page, in one move. Bank consents are revoked with each bank before erasure, then all your data is deleted: accounts, transactions, budgets, conversations and encrypted tokens.
home.faq.q4: Can I delete my account and my data?
home.faq.title: Common questions

home.security.lead: A service that reads bank accounts is judged on what it forbids itself.
home.security.s1.body: You enter them there, never here. Clair never sees them.
home.security.s1.title: Your credentials stay with your bank
home.security.s2.body: No transfer, no debit is possible. The authorisation is withdrawn at your bank or from a button here.
home.security.s2.title: Read-only, revocable
home.security.s3.body: The access your bank issues is stored encrypted with AES-256, under keys that can be rotated.
home.security.s3.title: Encrypted tokens
home.security.s4.body: Third-party names, IBANs and references are stripped before anything is sent. A transfer stays a transfer.
home.security.s4.title: Labels masked before the AI
home.security.title: Security first

tour.balances.body: The balance of each account, and the curve for the month. It reads at a glance: a steady slope is a normal month, a sharp drop signals a large debit.
tour.balances.title: Your balances, and how they move
tour.bank.body: The figures you have just seen are an example. Connect your bank and your last three months appear in their place, already sorted.
tour.bank.title: Over to you
tour.budgets.body: A limit per category, and where you stand. The red one is exceeded — the app tells you at the top of the page rather than waiting for you to notice.
tour.budgets.title: Your budgets
tour.categories.body: Your spending by category, largest first. Each category keeps its colour from one month to the next, so you recognise it without reading.
tour.categories.title: Where the money goes
tour.flows.body: Spending means nothing on its own: a thousand euros is a frugal month or a ruinous one depending on what came in. The bar shows the share of your income that has gone. On the right, what is still due before month end — known amounts on known dates, not estimates.
tour.flows.title: What comes in, what goes out
tour.metrics.body: What you have spent, what is left on your budgets, and how the month compares with previous ones. The third is the most useful: it says whether a month is out of the ordinary, or just like the others.
tour.metrics.title: The month in three figures
tour.nav.body: All your transactions with search and filters, the assistant to talk to about your spending, your budgets, and categorisation to correct a rule that gets it wrong.
tour.nav.title: The rest of the app
tour.subscriptions.body: Detected on their own, from operations that come back at the same rhythm for a stable amount. The app also flags those whose amount has gone up.
tour.subscriptions.title: Recurring payments
